whatis.h2: What counts as a procurement saving?
whatis.intro: A procurement saving is money a negotiation takes off what you pay suppliers, measured from a baseline price. A hard saving lowers the price on the invoice. Cost avoidance stops a rise that was on its way. Both count, but only the first shows up in spend.

cards.title: Lower prices on cases you already buy
cards.body: Lower prices on cases you were already buying, on the same terms. A new line has no old price to beat, so its first price is spend, not a saving.
cards.alt: Plus sign, for lower prices on cases you already buy

cards.title: Rebates, terms and free goods sit apart
cards.body: Rebates paid back later, better payment terms and free goods. Each can be worth real money, but each belongs on its own line, not in the case price.
cards.alt: Minus sign, for rebates, terms and free goods kept on their own lines

cards.title: Where a distributor's saving goes
cards.body: You resell what you buy. If the $1.44 a case goes straight into lower sell prices, your accounts keep the saving and your margin stays put.
cards.alt: Light bulb, for a saving passed on in sell prices

who.intro: Supplier negotiations at a food distributor end in a savings figure, and this is where buyers and finance test it. Anyone who reports a saving, checks one or signs off a renewal should run it.

look.h2: Test a saving before it goes in the report
look.intro: A savings figure is only as good as the comparison under it. These three checks catch the claims that look fine in a deck and fail in review.

steps.title: The same case on both prices
steps.body: $22.56 has to buy the same pack, brand and grade that $24.00 did. A smaller pack or a cheaper brand is a different product, not a saving.

steps.title: Cases bought at the new price
steps.body: The calculator assumes the new price ran all year. If the deal started partway through, enter only the cases bought since, not the full 72,000.

steps.title: An increase someone put in writing
steps.body: Cost avoidance needs a real ask, such as a supplier letter or a new price list. A rise you expected but were never quoted does not count, so set it to 0%.

vos.h2: Where VOS picks up after a supplier deal
vos.h3: Your sell price is where a saving lands
vos.body: VOS does not measure savings or deal with your suppliers. It comes in after the deal: each account orders from its own guide, at the prices you set. When a deal changes a sell price, you update the guides in the VOS admin platform.

next.h2: What to run after procurement savings
next.intro: A saving is one number from one negotiation. These three check the invoice, the delivered cost and the payment terms behind it.

cards.title: Check the invoice held the deal
cards.body: Compare the price on each invoice with your standard, per case and as a percent, and see what the gap is worth a year.
cards.alt: Calculator, for checking invoices against the agreed price

cards.title: Rank supplier offers on landed cost
cards.body: Before you book a lower case price as a saving, check that it still wins per unit once freight is in.
cards.alt: Right arrow, for ranking supplier offers on landed cost

cards.title: Price the payment terms too
cards.body: See what paying a supplier early is worth as a yearly rate, and what the case costs after discounts and freight.
